name: HyperEVM Mainnet
limits: This is a private copy of HyperEVM Mainnet: transactions confirm on the copy only and never appear on Hyperliquid or its explorers.
The copy keeps chain id 999, so a transaction signed for it is also valid on HyperEVM Mainnet. Use test keys that hold no mainnet assets.

The engine is Foundry anvil v1.8.5 with a 30,000,000 gas limit and one block type. There is no small and big block split, blocks are mined on demand, gas prices follow anvil's base fee, and the custom methods eth_bigBlockGasPrice, eth_usingBigBlocks and eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber are not served.

HyperCore is a local model chainsim keeps on the copy, not Hyperliquid's engine. up seeds the L1 block number, mark and oracle prices and asset info for the BTC, ETH, SOL and HYPE perps, token info for USDC and HYPE, spot info and spot price for HYPE/USDC, and one order book per seeded perp. Spot balance, position, withdrawable and margin summary reads answer from the copy's Core state for any user, with zeros for an account that has none. Any other query reverts with a chainsim reason until chainsim set <name> precompile seeds it.

chainsim applies CoreWriter actions and bridge transfers when a chainsim command runs on the fork. A transaction sent straight to the RPC port by forge, cast or a frontend takes effect on HyperCore at the next chainsim command on that fork, not on its own. A read inside the block of an action never sees its effect.

Modeled actions are limit orders on perps (GTC, IOC and ALO) matched against the order book snapshot and other orders resting on the copy, cancels by order id and by client order id, spot sends and USD class transfers. Other actions are recorded and decoded with no effect, so spot orders, vault transfers, staking, delegation and send asset change nothing.

Market rules are simplified. Fees are the base tier (0.045% taker, 0.015% maker) with no volume tiers, discounts or rebates. Maintenance margin is half the initial margin at the perp's maximum leverage, with no tiered margin tables. A liquidation closes every position of the account at the mark price at once, with no partial or backstop step, and a negative balance after it is reset to zero. Funding is paid every hour of the fork's clock at a fixed rate per perp. Isolated margin and the delay mainnet applies to orders are not modeled.

Prices move only through chainsim set <name> hypercore price and chainsim time <name> --replay. Resting orders fill when such a move crosses them, not when the book changes, and the L1 block number keeps its value from up. A replay mines one block per hourly candle, an hour apart from the fork's current time rather than at the candles' own dates.

Funding rates come from the last settled rate in fundingHistory at up, or the current rate from the info API for perps added later, and stay fixed until chainsim set <name> hypercore funding changes them.

Order books are snapshots from the Hyperliquid info API, taken at up or by chainsim set <name> hypercore book <coin> --live, and fills on the copy consume their depth. They do not follow the live market.

HYPE sent to 0x2222…2222 and a linked ERC-20 sent to its token system address credit HyperCore spot on the copy. A spot send to a system address credits the sender's EVM balance directly, with no system transaction. The CoreDepositWallet path for USDC is not modeled.

set hypercore mirror copies a mainnet account's perp positions, cross margin and spot balances from the info API as they are at that moment, and its HYPE and profile token balances on the EVM side. Positions in isolated margin are copied as cross.

The default public upstream answers every state read at its latest block, whatever block the read names. up --block with it exits 7, and set CHAINSIM_HYPEREVM_MAINNET_RPC to an archive provider URL to fork at an older block.
Accounts and storage the copy has not written are read from the upstream on first access, at the upstream's latest state, so a long session can read state newer than the fork block.

The default upstream allows 100 requests per minute per IP. up makes about 98 requests and set hypercore mirror about 9, so set CHAINSIM_HYPEREVM_MAINNET_RPC to a provider URL for heavier runs. The Hyperliquid info API takes 10 requests at up, about 3 per mirror and 1 per replay, and CHAINSIM_HYPERLIQUID_INFO replaces its URL.
App indexers and explorers read the public chain, so they do not show what happens on the copy.
